S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.

subtypes.Future Hopelessness: The persistent conviction that the future holds no possibility of improvement.
subtypes.Belief in Impossibility of Improvement: The belief that the current situation will absolutely not get better.
subtypes.Helpless Resignation: A state of helplessness and resignation, believing that nothing will change despite effort.
subtypes.Chronic Pessimism: A persistent tendency to view everything negatively and fail to consider positive possibilities.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (PDD), or dysthymia, is a chronic mood disorder characterized by a depressed mood lasting at least two years in adults, accompanied by additional depressive features and clinically significant distress or impairment. Compared with major depressive disorder, PDD tends to have a more insidious onset, a longer and more stable course, and symptoms that are less severe but more enduring, often becoming embedded in a person's sense of self. Patients frequently present with long‑standing low mood, low energy, and pessimism that they may describe as their "normal" way of being, leading to underrecognition and delayed treatment. Comorbidity with major depressive episodes (double depression), anxiety disorders, and medical conditions is common, and functional impairment can be substantial despite relatively mild to moderate symptom intensity at any given time.

patient.personality: Jieun is a quietly curious, highly organized person who seeks calm through mindful rituals and careful planning, yet tends to internalize worries about finances and health.
patient.stressor: A little over three years ago, Jieun and her spouse were hit with an unexpected combination of medical bills and a rent increase, just as a promising part‑time office job she was counting on fell through. Her plans to stabilize the household income with virtual‑assistant work and small Japanese cooking workshops kept getting delayed by technology hurdles, childcare demands, and her own growing self‑doubt, leaving her feeling increasingly stuck at home and dependent on her partner’s income. Over the ensuing years she became more isolated, spending long stretches alone organizing budgets, reading self‑help books, and trying to perfect every detail of a home‑based business that never seemed ready to launch, which eroded her confidence and sense of purpose despite yoga, tea ceremony, and hiking offering only brief relief. When she noticed that her meticulous attempts to “fix” their finances were no longer translating into action, and her spouse gently pointed out how disengaged and persistently downcast she had become, she agreed to see a psychiatrist at the suggestion of her primary care provider, who was concerned about her prolonged low mood and functional decline.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’ve been feeling down and empty for years now, like I just can’t shake this sadness.”

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days it feels like there’s a gray film over everything, so even when I’m doing things I usually enjoy, like making a careful cup of tea or planning a new bento recipe, there’s this dull, heavy sadness in the background that never really lifts, just varies in how strong it is.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: I wake up already feeling tired, like I’ve run a marathon in my sleep, and even simple things like answering emails about possible virtual-assistant work or tidying the apartment for the hundredth time feel weirdly exhausting, so I end up lying on the couch scrolling or staring at my budget spreadsheets without actually doing anything.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.
S083.manifestation: When I think about the future, I just assume we’ll always be scraping by and that my little business ideas will stay stuck in notebooks, so I catch myself thinking, ‘What’s the point of trying again?’ and then I just sort of give up before I even start, because I can’t imagine it turning out any differently than the last few years have.
